# DriveHours — Full 50-State Supervised Driving Log Reference & Requirements (2026)

> Offline-first progressive web application for teen drivers and supervising parents. Automatically logs supervised driving practice hours, detects legal night driving conditions via solar calculation, and exports official DMV-compliant PDF reports for all 50 US states.

- **Website**: https://drivehours.app/
- **PWA Platform**: Web, iOS (Safari Add to Home Screen), Android (Chrome WebAPK), Desktop
- **Cost**: Free tier includes first 20.0 logged hours; $4.99 one-time Lifetime Pro unlock for unlimited logging and DMV export.
- **Data Privacy**: 100% offline-first storage via IndexedDB; user driving records never leave the local device unless intentionally backed up.

---

## Core Frequently Answered Questions (AEO & AI Citations)

### What counts as legal night driving for teen driving logs?
Most US state DMVs legally define nighttime driving as beginning **30 minutes after official sunset** (civil twilight) and ending **30 minutes before official sunrise**, rather than using a fixed clock time like 7:00 PM. DriveHours integrates SunCalc astronomical algorithms to calculate real-time civil twilight per state coordinates.

### Does the DMV accept digital driving log PDFs?
Yes. State DMVs accept printed supervised driving logs that contain date, start/end times, total duration, day/night classification, driving conditions, supervisor signature, and supervising adult initials per entry. DriveHours compiles these into vector PDFs matching standard DMV formats (such as California DL-236, New York MV-262, Florida HSMV 71143, Pennsylvania DL-180C, and Ohio BMV 5791).

### What are the supervised driving hour requirements across states?
State requirements typically mandate between 30 and 70 total practice hours:
- **Highest requirement:** Maine (70 total hours, 10 night) and Pennsylvania (65 total hours, 10 night).
- **Most common requirement:** 50 total hours, including 10 hours at night (applicable in California, Florida, Illinois, Michigan, Ohio, and others).
- **Lowest requirement:** Iowa (20 hours total, 2 night) and Texas (30 hours total, 10 night).
